content.text:
cp -r

cp -r is a Unix/macOS command used to copy directories recursively.

Basic syntax
Bash
cp -r source_directory destination_directory
What it does

-r (recursive) means:

copy the folder

copy all subfolders

copy all files inside them

Examples

Copy a folder:

Bash
cp -r my_folder backup_folder

Copy into another directory:

Bash
cp -r my_folder /tmp/

Copy and rename destination:

Bash
cp -r my_folder my_folder_backup
Common useful flags

-v → verbose (shows what is being copied)

-i → interactive (asks before overwrite)

-p → preserve timestamps/permissions

Example:

Bash
cp -რივ my_folder backup_folder

If you want, I can also show:

safer modern alternative (rsync)

how to copy only changed files

or how it behaves with symlinks (-L, -P)
